AUTHOR: A. S. Srikanth; S. Thirandas; D. A. Balamuguran; A. Daga; R. Vincent; T. Padir; D. Saha
TITLE: Real-Time Background-Agnostic Fish Localization in Underwater Videos towards Autonomous Species Monitoring
REGION: Tweed River estuary and Tallebudgera Creek, SE Queensland, Australia; Ipswich Mills Dam fishway, Massachusetts, USA
SPECIES: luderick, Australian bream (Seagrass); river herring (IRWA); localization is fish vs background
DATA: Luderick-Seagrass dataset (4,281 frames, Ditria et al.) + IRWA river herring fishway camera (10 videos, ~1,200 manually labelled frames)
V_EV: Sec. V: 'the noise level was high, and the illumination was not so good as Seagrass.'
R_EV: Sec. V: SUIM-Net 'was not re-trained with manually labeled IRWA frames'; Table I: SUIM-Net F-score 81.25 (Seagrass) vs 31.65 (IRWA)
E_EV: Table I: only 'F-score and mean intersection over union (mIoU)' reported
ARCH: Ensemble (soft/weighted voting) of SuBSENSE background subtraction, fine-tuned SUIM-Net, and RLOF optical flow
NOTE: Seagrass split: 'all of the 4,281 frames were used for either one of training, validation, or testing' - unit/ratio not stated (D1=NR); results reported as validation accuracy. External test: SUIM-Net trained on 2,200 Seagrass images and applied unchanged to IRWA fishway (different country, camera, freshwater, background) - R1=Y, R2=복수. However the weighted-voting ensemble weights were trained on labelled IRWA frames, so the WV result itself is not fully external. V3=Y based on qualitative illumination statements (IR lights at night, poorer illumination at IRWA). Seagrass public; IRWA not shared.
